stories.headline: Wisbech St Mary Academy hosts fundraiser for annual firework display
stories.brief:
Pupils at Wisbech St Mary CofE Academy have held a special fundraising day to support the school’s upcoming Firework Spectacular. Children attended school in non-uniform and elaborate hairstyles to collect donations for the event's bottle stall. 

The Firework Spectacular is scheduled for Saturday, November 7, and has been a local tradition for over 40 years. Organisers say the event is open to the entire community, not just those with links to the school. Residents are encouraged to book tickets in advance to secure a discount before the November 6 deadline. Tickets are available online via TicketSource.

stories.headline: Volunteers help create new wildflower meadow in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Volunteers have joined West Norfolk Council staff to plant hundreds of native wildflower plugs at the Fairstead recreation ground in King’s Lynn. The project aims to transform the site into a diverse meadow to support local wildlife, including bees and butterflies. This work follows the earlier spreading of green hay to introduce native seeds to the area. 

The initiative is part of the council’s Pollinator Action Plan, which seeks to restore habitats across the borough. Officials say the lessons learned at the Fairstead site will help guide future nature recovery projects in West Norfolk. The council has thanked the Nature Volunteer Network for their assistance in establishing this new green space for the community.

stories.headline: Nine-hour weather warning issued for Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A weather warning is currently in place across Cambridgeshire as Storm Austen moves into the region. Forecasters have issued the alert for a nine-hour period. Residents are advised to stay updated on the latest conditions as the storm progresses.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire man avoids prison sentence amid jail overcrowding
stories.brief: A man from Lincolnshire has avoided a custodial sentence due to current prison overcrowding. The decision was reported by the BBC, noting that the capacity issues within the jail system influenced the outcome of the case. No further details regarding the individual or the nature of the offence have been released.

stories.headline: Police arrest following break-in at services
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest in connection with a break-in at a service station. Officers are currently investigating the incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual detained have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Weasenham Lane in Wisbech reopens following water main repairs
stories.brief:
Drivers in Wisbech can once again use Weasenham Lane. The road has reopened following repairs to a burst water main that had forced a closure for several days. 

Anglian Water confirmed that while the pipework was fixed earlier, the route remained shut to allow for necessary repairs to the road surface. The company has thanked local residents for their patience while the site was cleared. This incident marks the third time a water main has burst on this particular road in the last four months. The route is now operating as normal.

stories.headline: Police appeal following assault on 505 bus
stories.brief:
Lincolnshire Police are investigating an assault that took place on a 505 bus travelling between King’s Lynn and Sutton Bridge. Officers were called to Bridge Road in Sutton Bridge shortly after 6:05pm on Tuesday, October 20. 

Reports indicate a man behaved aggressively towards a girl on the service before tipping alcohol on her, pulling her hair, and removing her from her seat. A second girl was also assaulted during the incident. Police are urging anyone who was on the bus at the time to come forward. Witnesses should contact 101 and quote incident number 404 of October 20.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire’s forgotten railway stations highlighted
stories.brief: A recent report from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News has revisited the history of the county’s rail network. The publication has identified five railway stations across Cambridgeshire that are no longer in operation. The feature highlights these long-lost sites, which may be unfamiliar to many local residents today.

stories.headline: Council error halts school crossing plans
stories.brief: Plans for a new pedestrian crossing near local schools have been cancelled following an administrative mistake by the council. The project, which had been intended to improve safety for students in the area, will no longer go ahead due to the error. No further details regarding the nature of the mistake or potential future alternatives have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: West Winch woman charged following King’s Lynn bus station incident
stories.brief:
A 46-year-old woman from West Winch is due to appear in court following an arrest at King’s Lynn bus station. Paula Asker, of Coronation Avenue, has been charged with being drunk and disorderly. Police were alerted to the incident by CCTV operators at approximately 5pm on Tuesday. 

The charge comes as part of an ongoing effort by West Norfolk Police to tackle anti-social behaviour at the site. Officers have confirmed that Ms Asker has been bailed to appear at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, November 19. Police are continuing to monitor the area and are encouraging members of the public to report any concerns by calling 101, or 999 in an emergency.

stories.headline: Fenland students prepare for national skills competition
stories.brief:
Students from across the Fens have been recognised at a special event ahead of the WorldSkills UK national finals. Learners from March, Terrington St John, and Wisbech are among those representing the College of West Anglia in the competition, often described as the skills Olympics. 

The celebration at the King’s Lynn campus honoured students who progressed through regional heats to reach the finals this November. Local competitors include Erika Rimkus, Finn Mcauley, and Paige Marshall from Wisbech, Marc Watson from March, and Rianna Moore from Terrington St John. College principal David Pomfret praised the finalists, noting that they represent the top five percent of entrants in their respective vocational fields.

stories.headline: Looking back at October community events in the Fens
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at community highlights from across the region during past Octobers. In 2017, King’s Lynn hosted a Halloween Spooktacular at the Vancouver Quarter, while young artists were celebrated at Gaywood Library’s superhero drawing competition. That same year, a 24-hour spinathon at Lynnsport raised over one thousand pounds for the British Heart Foundation.

Looking further back to 2013, the Railway Arms in Downham Market was named the national cider pub of the year. Meanwhile, in Swaffham, the cemetery chapel was rededicated following a forty-five thousand pound renovation. These stories reflect a busy period of local activity, from charity fundraising and remembrance services to community celebrations held across our towns.

stories.headline: Peterborough council considers SEND reform to address budget gap
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council is looking at potential reforms to its Special Educational Needs and Disabilities services. The proposed changes are intended to help address a budget deficit currently standing at nine point nine million pounds. The local authority is exploring these measures as part of its ongoing financial planning.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn ambulance station hosts stem cell donor event
stories.brief:
Staff and volunteers at the King’s Lynn ambulance station are holding a stem cell swabbing event this Monday. The initiative aims to find a donor for Reuben, the ten-month-old son of a local paramedic, who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia. The East of England Ambulance Service is hosting the session to encourage more people to join the DKMS stem cell register.

Those aged between 16 and 55 can participate in the simple cheek swab test. Members of the public who are unable to attend the station can also support the appeal by requesting a home testing kit through the DKMS website. Every new registration increases the potential for finding a life-saving match for patients in need of a transplant.

stories.headline: Update on Whittlesey leisure centre plans
stories.brief: There has been a significant development regarding the proposed eighteen-point-seven million pound leisure centre in Whittlesey. Further details have been released concerning the project, which aims to bring new sporting and recreational facilities to the town. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local updates as the plans progress.

stories.headline: Fawkes in The Walks returns to King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn is preparing for the return of the Fawkes in The Walks fireworks display on Friday, November 6. Organised by West Norfolk Council, the event features fairground rides, food stalls, and live entertainment starting at 6pm. Radio West Norfolk’s Simon Rowe will host the evening, with the mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, leading the countdown to the fireworks at 8pm.

Entry to the park is free, though voluntary donations are encouraged to help cover costs. Attendees are reminded that private fireworks, sparklers, pets, and drones are not permitted. Visitors are also asked to support the event by purchasing glow products from authorised sellers on-site.

stories.headline: Optometry leaders urge sector to support global compact
stories.brief: The Association of Optometrists is calling for the eye care sector to join forces in support of a new global compact. Industry leaders are encouraging professionals across the field to unite behind the initiative. No further details regarding the specific aims of the compact or its impact on local services have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Funding boost for East Cambridgeshire residents in hardship
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council has confirmed it is receiving 110,000 pounds annually to provide support for local residents facing financial hardship. The funding is intended to assist those struggling with day-to-day costs. Further details regarding how the money will be distributed and who is eligible to apply for this assistance are expected to be released by the local authority in due course.

stories.headline: Met Office weather update for Long Sutton
stories.brief: The Met Office has issued a weather update for Long Sutton in Lincolnshire. Residents in the area are advised to check the latest forecasts for any potential changes in local conditions. Further information regarding the current weather outlook for the town is available through official Met Office channels.

stories.headline: Wisbech college hosts event to encourage young women into STEM careers
stories.brief:
Students from across the Fens have attended a special event at the College of West Anglia’s Green Skills Academy in Wisbech. The "Girls in STEM" day aimed to inspire young women to consider careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Pupils from Thomas Clarkson Academy in Wisbech and Neale-Wade Academy in March joined college students for practical activities, including virtual welding and thermal imaging. Representatives from various industries, including Anglian Water and Polypipe, were on hand to discuss career pathways. Organisers say the event was designed to challenge traditional gender stereotypes and highlight the growing need for a diverse workforce in sectors supporting a greener economy.

stories.headline: Nine new bus shelters installed across King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Nine new bus shelters have been installed in and around King’s Lynn following an £82,500 replacement programme. The project, funded by West Norfolk Council and a Norfolk County Council grant, replaces ageing structures that had suffered from damage and structural issues. 

New shelters are now located on Winston Churchill Drive, William Booth Road, Gayton Road, Saddlebow Road, Queen Mary Road, and Parkway. Officials say the modern replacements are expected to last for 25 years. By removing advertising and electrical connections from the previous sites, the council expects to recoup its investment within four and a half years.

stories.headline: Changes to opening hours at local leisure centre
stories.brief: Residents in the Spalding area are being advised of upcoming changes to the opening hours at their local leisure centre. While the facility will remain open for public use, the times at which visitors can access the site are set to be adjusted. Further details regarding the specific new operating schedule have not yet been confirmed. Users are encouraged to check for updates before planning their next visit to the centre.

stories.headline: East Anglia care staff honoured at Black Swan awards
stories.brief: Outstanding care workers from across East Anglia have been recognised for their dedication at the recent Black Swan Care Awards. The event celebrated the hard work and commitment of staff members working within the care sector throughout the region. The awards highlight the essential contributions made by these professionals in supporting residents and their families.

stories.headline: Half-term events and film screenings at The Light Cinema in Wisbech
stories.brief:
The Light Cinema at Cromwell Retail Park in Wisbech is hosting a variety of activities for the half-term break. A free Halloween vintage market takes place in the foyer this Saturday, October 24, between midday and 7pm. Families can also take part in an autumn trail throughout the week for a chance to win a prize. 

Younger children can attend a free slime-making session on October 30, though booking is required. The cinema is also screening a selection of family films and Halloween classics, with ticket prices starting from £5.75. Further details on all events, including the Disney Junior Cinema Club and special family film offers, are available on The Light Wisbech website.

stories.headline: Free electrical safety checks available in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Residents are invited to have their heated blankets, throws, and portable heaters tested for safety next month. Norfolk County Council Trading Standards and the Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service are hosting a drop-in event at King’s Lynn Library on Monday, November 2. Experts will be on hand between 10am and noon to test items and provide advice on fire safety and scam prevention. 

Last year, 60 percent of items brought to similar sessions failed safety checks. Residents are encouraged to bring items belonging to friends or neighbours who cannot attend. No booking is required for the session at the New Conduit Street library, and the service is free of charge.

stories.headline: Man named following sexual gratification recording charges
stories.brief: A man has been named following allegations that he recorded victims for the purpose of sexual gratification. The Ely Standard reports that the individual is facing charges related to these offences. No further details regarding the identity of the accused or the specific location of the alleged incidents have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: New housing development finished in Long Sutton
stories.brief: A total of 45 new homes have been completed in Long Sutton. The project was delivered by the housing association Accent. The development is now finished, according to reports from Housing Digital.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man charged following incident near nursery
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been named following an accusation of indecent exposure. The individual is alleged to have masturbated in a bush located outside a nursery. The report was published by Peterborough Matters. No further details regarding the identity of the man or the specific location of the nursery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Three Lincolnshire men jailed following shooting incident
stories.brief: Three men from Lincolnshire have been sentenced to prison following a shooting at a residential property. The house was occupied by a mother and her young child at the time of the incident. The details of the sentencing were reported by the Peterborough Telegraph.

stories.headline: Twelve road closures planned across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised of upcoming disruption on the county's road network. A total of twelve road closures are scheduled to take place throughout the week. Drivers are encouraged to check their routes before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works. Further details regarding the specific locations and timings of the affected roads can be found via local traffic reporting services.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Rotary Club pledges support for therapy room project
stories.brief:
The Rotary Club of King’s Lynn has promised to support a refurbishment project at the Mr Bee’s Family Centre. The pledge follows a presentation by Abbie Mulcairn from the charity Brave Futures, which provides specialist support to children and young people across Norfolk and Suffolk who have experienced sexual abuse.

During the meeting, the charity highlighted that referrals at their King’s Lynn centre have more than doubled over the past six months. Rotary club members heard that the organisation is currently managing high demand while navigating challenges within the criminal justice system. The club president confirmed they will assist with the planned improvements to the centre’s therapy room.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated by Huddersfield Town
stories.brief: Peterborough United suffered a four-one defeat away to Huddersfield Town. The result was confirmed following the latest round of fixtures.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for 34 new park homes in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A planning proposal has been put forward for the construction of 34 bungalow-style residential park homes in an East Cambridgeshire town. The development would see the new properties built to provide additional housing in the area. No further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: New career for former roofer at HMP Whitemoor
stories.brief: A former roofer has begun a new career at HMP Whitemoor. The individual, who previously worked in the roofing trade, has now taken up a position at the prison facility. No further details regarding the nature of the role or the start date have been released.

stories.headline: University Centre West Anglia students celebrate graduation in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Fifty-nine students from the University Centre West Anglia marked the completion of their degrees during a ceremony at Lynn Minster on Saturday, October 10. The graduates, who studied subjects ranging from Computer Science to Primary Education, took part in a traditional academic procession through the town centre following the formal proceedings. 

During the event, Emma Claridge received the Outstanding Student Award for her work in Primary Education. University officials highlighted the importance of providing local higher education opportunities to support the skills needs of employers across the region. The celebrations concluded with a gathering at the Lynn campus for graduates, their families, and staff.

stories.headline: Residents report sewage smell in Cambridgeshire market town
stories.brief: People living in a Cambridgeshire market town are reporting a persistent and unpleasant odour. According to recent reports, the area is currently being affected by what has been described as a foul stench of sewage. No further details regarding the source or the specific location of the smell have been confirmed at this time.

stories.headline: Campaign group considers cash rewards for information on child abusers
stories.brief: A campaign group led by a father is exploring the possibility of offering financial rewards for information regarding child abusers. The initiative is being developed as part of the organisation's latest project. Further details on how the scheme might operate have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Harding’s Pits in South Lynn granted village green status
stories.brief:
A long-running campaign to protect Harding’s Pits in South Lynn has reached a successful conclusion. Norfolk County Council has officially approved the site for village green status, following a proposal submitted by West Norfolk Council earlier this year. 

The designation provides statutory protection against development and encroachment, ensuring the land remains available for community use. This decision marks the end of a process spanning more than 30 years, which began with an initial application by the Lynn 2,000 lobby group. Local campaigners and councillors have welcomed the news, noting that the status will safeguard the area’s natural habitats and public open space for future generations.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn students design new logo for local educational charity
stories.brief:
Graphic design students from the College of West Anglia have been recognised for their work on a new logo challenge. Armanda Rakstys, Chloe Wilson, and Kian Moon were tasked with creating a visual identity for the West Norfolk and King’s Lynn Girls’ Schools Trust. The project required the Level 3 students to reflect the charity’s history and its commitment to supporting education for girls and young women in the region. 

The trust, which was established in 1983, manages funds from the former West Norfolk and King’s Lynn High School for Girls. College staff and trust representatives praised the students for their research, professionalism, and creative approach to the brief.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire District Council seeks devolution pilot
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council is challenging plans for Local Government Reorganisation. The authority has formally called for a devolution pilot to be introduced instead. The move comes as the council seeks to address proposed changes to local administrative structures. No further details regarding the timeline or the specific nature of the pilot scheme have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Planning appeal granted for 152 new homes in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A housing development of 152 dwellings in Cambridgeshire has been given the go-ahead following a successful planning appeal. The project, which was previously stalled, will now proceed after the decision was overturned. Further details regarding the specific location of the site or the timeline for construction have not yet been released. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local planning portals for any upcoming updates regarding the development's progress.

stories.headline: Wisbech teenager to be sentenced for park knife attack
stories.brief:
An eighteen-year-old man from Wisbech is due to be sentenced next month following a knife attack in a local park. Densias Griaitis, of The Lawns, was found guilty at Peterborough Magistrates' Court last Tuesday. He was convicted of grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon.

The charges follow an incident at Wisbech Park on August 20 last year, where a sixteen-year-old boy was wounded. Griaitis has been remanded on conditional bail and is scheduled to appear at Cambridge Crown Court for sentencing on November 17.

stories.headline: Wisbech councillors urge police to tackle traffic and anti-social behaviour
stories.brief:
Wisbech Town Council is calling for increased police enforcement following reports of local concerns. During Monday’s meeting, Councillor Dal Roy highlighted that heavy goods vehicles are ignoring a seven-and-a-half-ton weight limit to use Coalwharf Road and South Brink as a shortcut before 7am.

Separately, Councillor Sidney Imafidon raised issues regarding the footpath between Lynn Road and Clarence Road. He reported a rise in anti-social behaviour, including noise, littering, and drug use. Councillor Imafidon stated that while police have attended the area following his previous reports, the problems remain unresolved. Councillors are now urging officers to take further action to address these ongoing issues for local residents.

stories.headline: Dersingham care home retains good CQC rating
stories.brief:
The Gables Residential Home in Dersingham has successfully maintained its ‘good’ rating from the Care Quality Commission. Following an unannounced inspection on August 3, the facility was assessed across five key categories, including safety, leadership, and the effectiveness of its care.

While inspectors praised the home’s high standards and strong leadership, the report also identified areas for improvement. Suggestions included enhancing the communal environment, improving garden accessibility, and addressing concerns regarding potential social isolation for residents. Registered manager Stephanie Durham expressed pride in the team’s achievement and thanked the local community for their ongoing support in helping the home continue to meet its service standards.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire District Council seeks social care powers
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council is calling for new responsibilities regarding local social care services. The request was reported by the Local Government Chronicle, highlighting the council's interest in taking on a greater role in the sector. No further details regarding the specific nature of the proposed changes or the timeline for any potential transition have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Man arrested following knife incident in Spalding town centre
stories.brief: Police have arrested a man following reports that people were threatened with a knife in Spalding town centre. Officers were called to the scene to deal with the incident. An investigation into the matter is now underway.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for Christmas Day arsonist
stories.brief: A person has been jailed following an arson incident that took place on Christmas Day. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the sentencing today. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech Mayor highlights recent community engagements
stories.brief:
The Mayor of Wisbech, Councillor Lucie Foice-Beard, has provided an update on her recent community activities during Monday night’s town council meeting. Over the past month, the Mayor attended various local events, including the National Heritage Open Days, a harvest lunch at All Saints Church, and visits to the Alan Hudson Centre and The Ferry Project.

Looking ahead, the Mayor is preparing for several upcoming local initiatives. These include a free Halloween event at The Spinney on October 28, the Christmas Golden Ages event on November 11, and the town’s Christmas lights switch-on scheduled for November 29. Councillor Foice-Beard also noted that the High Sheriff, Francis Burkitt, is expected to return to Wisbech at the end of October.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Soroptimists host guest speaker Anna Mudeka
stories.brief:
Members of Soroptimist International King’s Lynn recently welcomed musician, actress, and educator Anna Mudeka as their guest speaker. Ms Mudeka, who is also a Deputy Lord Lieutenant of Norfolk, shared her life story through song and traditional performance. During her talk, she discussed her career in music, her work with The Mudeka Foundation supporting disadvantaged children in Zimbabwe, and her current business ventures.

In other club news, a recent quiz night held at South Wootton Village Hall raised nearly £400 for local charities. The group’s next event will be a charity literary lunch taking place on November 15. Further details regarding the club’s activities can be found on the Soroptimist International King’s Lynn website.

stories.headline: Family pays tribute to Yaxley motorcyclist following fatal Sawtry collision
stories.brief:
The family of 23-year-old Tyler Ellis from Yaxley has paid tribute to him following a fatal collision on the B1043 Old North Road at Sawtry. Mr Ellis was riding a black Kawasaki motorcycle when it collided with a red Volvo HGV at approximately 12:50pm on Monday, October 5. He passed away at Addenbrooke’s Hospital the following day.

The 76-year-old lorry driver from Wisbech was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has since been released on bail until January 4. Cambridgeshire Constabulary is continuing to appeal for witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage of the incident to come forward by calling 101 or visiting the force's website.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Rotary club donates £500 to support Kolkata street children
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn couple has received a £500 donation from the local Priory Rotary Club to support The Hope Foundation for Street Children. Dr Prabir Mitra and his wife Sanjukta recently completed a 111-day, 28,200-mile road journey from King’s Lynn to Kolkata. 

The pair travelled through Europe, Central Asia, China, Tibet, and Nepal, crossing 20 international borders. During the trip, they raised awareness about diabetes and collected funds for a dialysis unit at The Hope Hospital in Kolkata. The Rotary donation will assist the foundation in providing education and protection for street children. The couple faced numerous challenges during their expedition, including difficult road conditions and frequent border closures.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage comments on Peterborough United draw
stories.brief: Robbie Savage has offered praise following Peterborough United’s recent draw against Burton Albion. The assessment of the match performance comes as the club continues its current campaign. No further details regarding the fixture or upcoming matches have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire seeks devolution deal
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council is pursuing a devolution deal without the need for Local Government Reorganisation. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the local authority is seeking to secure new powers and funding arrangements while maintaining its current administrative structure. No further details regarding the proposed timeline or the specific nature of the devolution bid have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Police appeal following quad bike theft
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are asking for the public's help following the theft of a quad bike. Officers have launched an appeal for information regarding the incident. Anyone who may have witnessed suspicious activity or who has relevant details is being urged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Weasenham Lane in Wisbech closed following burst water main
stories.brief:
Drivers in Wisbech are facing further disruption on Weasenham Lane. The road is currently closed following a burst water main that occurred over the weekend. Anglian Water has confirmed that repairs to the pipe are finished, but the route remains shut while crews work to fix the damaged road surface. 

This marks the third time in four months that the road has been closed due to a burst main. Anglian Water says the closure will remain in place until it is safe for traffic to return. The company has thanked local residents for their patience while these essential repairs are completed.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn singer Adam Tucker exits The Voice UK
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn singer Adam Tucker has left The Voice UK following the show’s latest battle round. Adam, who provided the singing voice for Robbie Williams in the 2024 biopic Better Man, performed a duet of the Goo Goo Dolls' hit ‘Iris’ alongside fellow contestant Jack Algar. 

Coaches Danny Jones and Tom Fletcher praised the performance, noting that it was a positive opportunity for the singer to showcase his own vocal style. Although Adam did not progress to the semi-finals, he has described the public response to his performance as amazing. Adam previously impressed the judges during his blind audition with a rendition of the Robbie Williams song ‘Feel’.

stories.headline: Wigan man fined following assault at King’s Lynn nightclub
stories.brief:
A holidaymaker has been ordered to pay compensation and fines after assaulting a security guard in King’s Lynn. Forty-nine-year-old Matthew Crompton, from Wigan, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He admitted to a charge of assault by beating following an incident at Dr Thirsty’s nightclub on Norfolk Street in the early hours of Sunday, September 6.

The court heard that Crompton, who was visiting the area, punched a member of door staff in the face after being ejected from the venue. His solicitor stated that the punch was intended for a different guard. Crompton must pay £300 in compensation, a £750 fine, a £300 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

stories.headline: Delays expected for revamped leisure centre
stories.brief: Residents in the Fens may face a significant wait before they can use their local leisure centre. Reports indicate that the facility, which is currently undergoing a revamp, could remain closed for up to two years. No further details regarding the specific location or the reasons for the extended timeline have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Second man charged following Cambridgeshire burglaries
stories.brief: A second man has been charged in connection with a series of burglaries across Cambridgeshire. The charges follow a recent spate of incidents reported throughout the county. Police have confirmed the development as the investigation into the offences continues.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire regeneration plans approved
stories.brief: A major regeneration project aimed at improving towns across Lincolnshire has been officially approved. The ambitious vision, which focuses on development and local improvements, has now been given the green light. Further details regarding the specific towns involved and the timeline for these works are expected to follow as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following bus incident in Peterborough
stories.brief: A health and safety investigation is underway after a young boy fell from a double-decker bus in Peterborough. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the condition of the child or the specific location of the event have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New online radio station launches for the Fens
stories.brief: A new independent online radio station, Fenland Angels Radio, has officially launched. Operating 24 hours a day, the station aims to serve Wisbech and the wider Fens, including parts of West Norfolk. Founded by Nathaniel Daw, the service focuses on music, local stories, and community engagement. The team is currently developing its coverage of local events and interviews, and is inviting members of the public to get involved and develop their broadcasting skills. While the station is currently available online, the team is exploring future options for DAB broadcasting. Listeners can access the station through its website.

stories.headline: Man charged following incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station
stories.brief:
A 34-year-old man has been charged with assaulting three police officers following an incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station. Reuben Skinner, of Checker Street in Lynn, faces three counts of assault after officers were called to reports of a man with a head injury on Saturday evening. 

Police have confirmed that no weapons were involved in the incident, dismissing online speculation regarding a stabbing. Mr Skinner was arrested at the station and later taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital for treatment. He has been released on bail and is due to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 19. Enquiries into how the man sustained his initial injury remain ongoing.

stories.headline: Potential housing for asylum seekers in Fenland
stories.brief: Reports suggest that Fenland could potentially accommodate up to 200 asylum seekers. The information, which originated from the BBC, is currently being discussed regarding the possibility of housing this number of people within the district. No further details have been confirmed at this stage regarding specific locations or timelines for such a proposal. We will continue to monitor the situation for any updates that may affect local residents.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Women climb National League table
stories.brief: Peterborough United Women are enjoying a successful run of form. The team is currently moving up the National League standings, reaching a series of notable milestones during their recent campaign.

stories.headline: Plans revealed for major wind farm project in Shippea Hill
stories.brief: A new wind farm development has been proposed for Shippea Hill. The project is estimated to cost more than £100 million. Further details regarding the scale and timeline of the construction are expected to emerge as the planning process continues. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local planning portals for updates on how this significant infrastructure investment might impact the surrounding area.

stories.headline: Fifteen road closures announced across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised of fifteen separate road closures taking place throughout this week. The disruptions, reported by Peterborough Matters, may affect travel plans for those commuting across the county. Drivers are encouraged to check their routes before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works. No specific locations or durations for the closures have been provided at this time, so residents are urged to remain alert for local signage and traffic updates while travelling in the area.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports extend unbeaten streak to ten matches
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports have reached a ten-game unbeaten run following their latest fixture. Despite the positive result, the club’s manager has expressed frustration regarding the team's performance. The side continues its campaign amidst a busy schedule of midweek non-league football matches across the region.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire foster carers recognised for long service
stories.brief: More than 50 foster carers from across Cambridgeshire have been formally honoured for their dedication. Collectively, the group has provided 450 years of service to the local community. The recognition highlights the significant contribution these individuals have made to the lives of children in care throughout the region.

stories.headline: Air ambulance called to Long Sutton
stories.brief: An air ambulance has landed in Long Sutton. The incident was reported by the Fenland Citizen. No further details regarding the nature of the emergency or the condition of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over dust levels at Saxon Pit in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Residents in Whittlesey are raising concerns regarding dust emissions at the Saxon Pit site. Reports indicate that the situation has led to claims involving the use of public funds. Local authorities are currently facing scrutiny over the management of the site and the potential impact of the dust on the surrounding area. Further details regarding the nature of these claims and any planned action remain under discussion. We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available for the community.

stories.headline: Peterborough village may get new milk vending machine
stories.brief: Plans are being considered for the installation of a milk vending machine in a Peterborough village. The proposal, reported by the Peterborough Fenland Edge News, suggests the facility could soon be available to local residents. No specific location or start date for the service has been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: A10 Cambridge to Ely upgrade plans removed from project list
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade the A10 between Cambridge and Ely have been removed from the official list of road projects. The decision has been met with disappointment following the announcement. The route remains a key transport link for commuters and residents travelling across the region. No further details regarding the future of the scheme have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: March business claims lack of belief hinders black entrepreneurs
stories.brief: A company based in March has highlighted the challenges facing black business owners. According to the firm, known as Rayo, a lack of belief is currently holding back entrepreneurs from the black community. The business shared these views regarding the obstacles faced by black-owned enterprises in the region.

stories.headline: Dispute continues over Aldreth bus services
stories.brief: A disagreement regarding bus services in Aldreth remains unresolved. Despite the submission of letters and a petition from the public, the issue has led to a heated exchange involving the Mayor. Reports indicate that the Mayor has publicly challenged the accuracy of claims made by those involved in the dispute. No further details regarding the specific nature of the service changes or the next steps for the campaign have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Obituary notice for Long Sutton resident Rex Richardson
stories.brief: An obituary has been published for Rex Richardson, a resident of Long Sutton in Lincolnshire. The notice, which appeared in the Spalding Guardian, commemorates the life of Mr. Richardson following his passing in 2020. No further details regarding his life or funeral arrangements have been provided in the public record.

stories.headline: Funds raised for Fenland man in Spanish hospital
stories.brief: A fundraising appeal has reached three thousand pounds to support a Fenland man currently receiving treatment in a Spanish hospital. The individual, described as a deeply loved member of the community, is reported to be fighting for his life. Further details regarding the man's identity or the specific circumstances of his hospitalisation have not been released. The funds were gathered to assist with his ongoing care while he remains abroad.

stories.headline: Mayor suggests Peterborough university road project remains a possibility
stories.brief: The Mayor has indicated that plans for a new road serving the university in Peterborough could still go ahead. While details remain limited, the comments suggest the infrastructure project is still under consideration by local authorities. Further updates on the proposal are expected as discussions continue regarding the development of the university site and its surrounding transport links.

stories.headline: New £110,000 annual fund launched for Cambridgeshire families
stories.brief: A new financial support scheme has been announced for families across Cambridgeshire. Council leader Rayo confirmed that a fund worth £110,000 per year is being established to provide timely assistance to local households. The initiative aims to offer support to those in need throughout the region.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man charged following incident near nursery
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been named following an accusation of indecent exposure. The individual is alleged to have masturbated in a bush located outside a nursery. The report was published by Peterborough Matters. No further details regarding the identity of the man or the specific location of the nursery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: MasterChef star returns to King’s Lynn for special menu
stories.brief:
MasterChef: The Professionals semi-finalist Polly Norman has returned to her roots in Norfolk for two special evenings at King’s Lynn Golf Club. The 24-year-old from Upwell, who began her career at the club as a teenager, teamed up with head chef Liam Nicol to prepare a four-course menu featuring local game and coastal produce. 

Polly, who now works at Simpson’s in the Strand in London, previously worked as an assistant professional at the golf club before pursuing a culinary career. She says she hopes to eventually return to the county permanently to open her own gastropub on the Norfolk coast.

stories.headline: Deliberate rubbish fire reported in Fenland
stories.brief: Fire crews have attended an incident involving burning rubbish near a road in the Fens. Officials have confirmed that the blaze was started deliberately. No further details regarding the exact location or any potential damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Public invited to share views on future of Norfolk hospital services
stories.brief:
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group has launched a new campaign titled Case for Change. The initiative aims to plan how hospital care is delivered across the region for future generations. While officials state that no decisions regarding service changes have been made, they are encouraging the public to share their experiences via an independent Healthwatch survey. The survey remains open until Friday, November 6.

In other news, the Queen Elizabeth Hospital recently held its annual Team QEH Awards, presenting 14 prizes to staff members. Additionally, the hospital has begun its seasonal flu vaccination campaign for staff, urging those eligible to get protected ahead of the winter months. Further details on the survey can be found on the group's website.

stories.headline: Peterborough United fans react to Robbie Savage appointment
stories.brief: Supporters of Peterborough United have expressed enthusiasm following the appointment of Robbie Savage as the club's new manager. Fans are welcoming the change in leadership, with many describing the team’s current style of play as a return to the club's reputation for being great entertainers.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire District Council leader seeks devolution pilot status
stories.brief: The leader of East Cambridgeshire District Council, Councillor Anna Bailey, has formally requested that the government designate the region as a devolution pilot area. The proposal aims to secure greater local control over decision-making and resources for the district. Councillor Bailey has outlined her reasons for pursuing this status, suggesting that a pilot scheme would benefit the area by allowing for more tailored governance. Further details regarding the potential impact of this move on local services and administration are expected as the request is considered by central government officials.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pensioner remanded in custody
stories.brief: A 74-year-old resident from Long Sutton has been remanded in custody. The decision was made following a court appearance at Lincoln Magistrates’ Court. No further details regarding the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Potential plans for two new wind farms in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Proposals have emerged for the construction of two large-scale wind farms. The projects are earmarked for locations within Cambridgeshire and along the county border. Further details regarding the specific sites or the timeline for these developments have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Campaign launches to improve child visibility as clocks go back
stories.brief:
A new safety initiative, Be Bright Be Seen, is offering thousands of free reflective keyrings to schools, youth groups, and sports clubs across the region. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign aims to help children remain visible to motorists as the nights draw in. With the clocks changing this Sunday, October 25, organisers are encouraging the use of reflective gear and bright clothing for pedestrians and cyclists.

Teachers and youth leaders can apply for an allocation of the keyrings online at the Fenland Citizen website. Applications close this Sunday. The campaign follows recent national data highlighting a rise in road traffic injuries, emphasising the importance of staying visible during the darker winter months.

stories.headline: South Lynn man admits assault following domestic dispute
stories.brief:
A 48-year-old man from South Lynn has pleaded guilty to common assault at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Cornelius Doddy, of Wisbech Road, admitted to threatening his ex-partner with an ironing board during an argument on July 29. The court heard that the dispute began in a car and continued at their home, where the defendant was reportedly intoxicated. No injuries were sustained during the incident.

In mitigation, the court was told that tensions regarding a potential restaurant venture had contributed to the disagreement. Magistrates have ordered a pre-sentence report, and Mr Doddy has been released on conditional bail. He is due to return to court for sentencing on December 1.

stories.headline: Water supply disruption reported in Littleport
stories.brief:
Residents in Littleport are currently experiencing a loss of water supply following a burst water main. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the incident has left homes and businesses in the area without water. 

Engineers are working to address the issue, though a timeline for when supplies will be fully restored has not yet been confirmed. Those living in the affected area are advised to check local updates for further information as the situation develops.

stories.headline: Long Sutton travel agents prepare for Santa
stories.brief: Staff at a travel agency in Long Sutton have been busy preparing for the festive season by packing a suitcase for Santa Claus. The local team organised the special display to mark the arrival of Christmas. Residents in the area can view the festive luggage at the branch as part of their seasonal preparations.

stories.headline: Seven-year-old boy dies following incident in Wimblington
stories.brief: A seven-year-old boy has died following reports of a child in the water at Wimblington. Emergency services were called to the scene to respond to the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Rail disruption reported between Peterborough and Doncaster
stories.brief: Passengers travelling by rail this Sunday are being advised of disruption to LNER services. The issues are affecting the line running between Peterborough and Doncaster. Those planning to travel on this route are encouraged to check their journey details before setting off, as the service alterations may impact travel times across the region.

stories.headline: Anglian Water issues update on East Cambridgeshire supply problems
stories.brief:
Residents in East Cambridgeshire are facing ongoing water supply issues today. Anglian Water has released an update regarding the situation, though specific details on the cause or the number of affected properties remain limited. The utility company is currently working to resolve the disruption across the region. 

Customers are advised to check the Anglian Water website for the latest information and updates on when their service is expected to return to normal. We will bring you more on this story as further details become available.

stories.headline: Company denies environmental charges in Long Sutton
stories.brief: A company is contesting environmental charges relating to two sites in Long Sutton. The firm has entered formal denials regarding the allegations brought against them. No further details regarding the nature of the charges or the identity of the business have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Ten road closures planned across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised to plan their journeys carefully over the coming days. A total of ten road closures are scheduled to take place across the county throughout this week. Drivers are encouraged to check local travel updates before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works.

stories.headline: West Norfolk schools support mental health campaign
stories.brief:
Pupils and staff across several West Norfolk schools have marked World Mental Health Day by taking part in the ‘Hello Yellow’ campaign. Participants wore bright colours to raise awareness and funds for the charity Young Minds. At West Lynn Primary School, children and staff held a special assembly and completed mental health-related classroom activities. 

Other schools within the West Norfolk Academies Trust also joined the initiative, including Smithdon High School in Hunstanton, St Clement’s High School in Terrington St Clement, and Clenchwarton Primary. The schools shared donation links via their newsletters and websites to support the charity’s work. West Lynn Primary typically raises around £200 for the cause during this annual event.

stories.headline: Two men released following imitation firearm arrest
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have released two men without charge following an investigation into an imitation firearm. Officers had previously arrested the pair in connection with the incident. No further action will be taken against them.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man in critical condition in Spain
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire is currently in a coma and fighting for his life while in Spain. Reports indicate the individual is receiving medical treatment abroad, though no further details regarding his identity or the circumstances surrounding his condition have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services respond to river incident in King's Lynn
stories.brief:
Emergency crews were called to the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn on Saturday afternoon following reports of a person in the water. The alarm was raised by the local ferry team at 3:04pm. By the time the Hunstanton Coastguard Rescue Team arrived at South Quay, the individual had been recovered from the river and was receiving medical attention from paramedics. 

The incident involved a multi-agency response, including the East of England Ambulance Service, Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, and Norfolk Constabulary. Once the person was confirmed safe, all teams were stood down. The Coastguard is reminding the public to dial 999 and ask for the Coastguard if they spot anyone in difficulty along the coast.
